confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from six web searches (one RBA search and five price searches). The price results were mostly search-result snippets from aggregators with mixed dates and noticeably different figures. I did not open the underlying pages. Beer and cappuccino rest mainly on an Expat Arrivals table described in the results as July 2026 averages (about ARS 6,000 for a 500ml draft beer and ARS 6,100 for a cappuccino). Numbeo-derived and other figures were lower, at about ARS 5,200 for a cappuccino. I converted pesos to USD at roughly ARS 1,450 per USD. That rate is implied by the Expatistan figures, not an official rate I looked up. Peso prices and the peso's real exchange rate move quickly, so USD values could be off by 15-20%. The inexpensive-meal anchor is a bounded estimate from lunch-menu and Numbeo-style figures of about ARS 15,000-21,000. The two-person mid-range anchor is a bounded estimate from a roughly ARS 78,000 expat-area Italian dinner for two that included wine, which I adjusted for no drinks. The cocktail anchor uses the Expatistan average of about ARS 13,200, which is roughly US$9. The wine-glass anchor is not directly sourced. It uses a 2025 Buenos Aires Herald mid-range glass price of about ARS 5,000 and a typical wine-glass-to-beer ratio of about 1.1. All four accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge of Buenos Aires tourism pricing. I did not search for accommodation or inspect any booking pages or listings. They are the least certain anchors, and prices vary with neighborhood (Palermo, Recoleta and San Telmo are higher), season and whether the price quoted is the official or the parallel-market rate.
comparable_city_reasoning: No comparable city was used. Estimates are based on Buenos Aires price data and local peso-to-USD conversion. Buenos Aires is now expensive relative to other Latin American capitals, so I judged it closer to Santiago or Montevideo than to Lima or Bogotá.
